record.title: Authenticated pattern detail/preview expose markup by design; plan gating applies to selection and render, not catalog reads
record.description: Verified the authorization shape: DesignPatternViewSet is routed at /api/design/patterns/ and list/retrieve/preview are reachable by any authenticated non-staff user because get_permissions only special-cases 'default' (AllowAny) and writes (IsAdminUser), leaving IsAuthenticated for reads. The list serializer omits html/css/js while the detail serializer includes them, and the preview action returns rendered html/css plus raw pattern.js with no profile_has_benefit or allowed_templates_of check. However the claimed missing plan gate is not a trust-boundary violation on current source: the serializers and viewset docstrings state catalog reads are for any authenticated user, tests codify an owner without a plan reading detail markup and preview, the public /design/catalog/ endpoint already serves all pattern metadata plus the default pattern through the detail serializer, and the frontend intentionally loads the full catalog and gates only selection/apply via templateAllowed/allowed_templates. Entitlement is enforced where it matters: customization PATCH discards template/template_draft outside allowed_templates_of, allowed_templates_of maps DesignPattern tiers to has_design_plus/has_design_advanced, and render_store_pattern re-checks the stored template against the current plan with a default fallback. Retrieved markup is sanitized for document/srcdoc serving and the preview modal mounts it in a sandboxed iframe without allow-same-origin. The residual is at most an IP/business-policy question about premium template source, which is hardening (e.g., markup-free detail for non-entitled users), not a demonstrated security boundary crossing.
record.claimed_root_cause: Design pattern retrieve and preview are gated only by IsAuthenticated with no tier/benefit check, so premium/imported html/css/js is readable by every authenticated account even though applying the same designs is plan-gated.

trace.description: router.register(r'design/patterns', DesignPatternViewSet) exposes retrieve and the custom preview action under /api/design/patterns/<slug>/ and /preview/.

action 'default' -> AllowAny, create/update/partial_update/destroy -> IsAdminUser, everything else falls through to permission_classes=[IsAuthenticated]; retrieve and preview therefore require only authentication.

Detail serializer exposes id/slug/tier/template/layout/html/css/js/variables/tokens/preview/style etc.; the list serializer at lines 168-185 deliberately omits html/css/js and only exposes has_markup.

preview resolves self.get_object() (active-only for non-staff) and returns preview_pattern(pattern, theme, accent, style); there is no profile_has_benefit/allowed_templates_of/tier check on this path.

REFUTED impact: applying a design is plan-gated (allowed_templates_of at services.py:80-109; PATCH discards template/template_draft outside the whitelist at viewset.py:1425-1430; render_store_pattern re-checks at pattern_render.py:1766-1773 and style.id at 1799-1807). Catalog read is documented/tested as authenticated-catalog behavior, not a protected-content boundary.

evidence.description: Module docstring: 'Lectura del catálogo para cualquier usuario autenticado' and 'el detalle sí [manda HTML/CSS/JS], que es lo que aplica el front' — authenticated detail markup is the documented contract.
permission_classes=[IsAuthenticated] with get_permissions special-casing only default/writes; non-staff queryset filters is_active=True at lines 45-49.

Public /design/catalog/ is AllowAny+PublicReadThrottle and returns the default pattern via DesignPatternSerializer (detail, including markup when present) plus markup-free lists for all active patterns/styles.
test_list_hides_code_and_detail_returns_it and test_pattern_preview_renders_sample_data authenticate a plain owner and assert detail/preview return markup — codifying authenticated-catalog reads.
useDesignCatalog loads the shared catalog once for public web and Studio; frontend architecture treats the catalog as browsable by users with selection gated separately.

patternOptions/styleOptions include all active catalog rows; templateAllowed/allowedTemplatesFor disable selection for out-of-plan templates while the preview button calls designApi.patternPreview for the current pattern.
Preview modal mounts the returned document in an iframe with sandbox='allow-scripts allow-popups allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox' and no allow-same-origin.

allowed_templates_of derives store-design entitlement from plan benefits: has_customization for base, has_design_plus for plus, has_design_advanced for advanced, and active DesignPattern slugs by tier.

render_store_pattern re-checks customization.template against _allowed_templates_safe and falls back to the catalog default when the stored design left the plan; site_theme.style.id is re-checked against allowed templates at lines 1799-1807.
Seed loads pattern markup from seed_data.json or StoreApp/domains/design/sources/<slug>.html into DesignPattern.html/css/js — catalog assets generated/curated by the platform, not per-store secrets.

record.reason: The missing benefit check on catalog detail/preview is real but intended and bounded: the read contract is explicitly 'any authenticated user', tests and the public catalog already expose catalog metadata and default-pattern markup, and the frontend treats premium patterns as browsable upsell material with selection/apply enforced server-side by allowed_templates_of and render_store_pattern. No secret, credential, PII, or unauthorized rendered capability is exposed by retrieving sanitized markup; rendering is sandboxed/CSP-controlled. Treating premium template source as confidential IP would be a product/licensing policy decision requiring a markup-free serializer for non-entitled users — hardening, not a demonstrated trust-boundary violation.

record.title: Pattern preview is a bounded per-request render already constrained by the global authenticated user throttle; absent dedicated scope/cache is hardening, not a demonstrated DoS
record.description: Verified the request path: GET /api/design/patterns/<slug>/preview/ is a detail action on DesignCatalogViewSet. get_throttles only special-cases action 'default' to PublicReadThrottle; preview falls through to DRF DEFAULT_THROTTLE_CLASSES (ResilientAnonRateThrottle + ResilientUserRateThrottle). For an authenticated caller AnonRateThrottle returns no key and UserRateThrottle keys on request.user.pk with DEFAULT_THROTTLE_RATES['user']='1000/day'. There is no dedicated preview scope and no server-side preview cache (catalog_cached is used only for catalog/default payloads). The render itself is bounded: DesignPatternSerializer validates html/css/js to CODE_MAX=200_000 chars each, preview_pattern uses a fixed small sample context and constant sample fragments, sanitizes markup/css, and returns at most the stored markup size plus bounded theme CSS — there is no DB fan-out, external call, cache-stamp amplification, or output multiplier. The frontend calls the endpoint on demand from the picker. A dedicated throttle/cache would be defense-in-depth, but source does not show a trust-boundary violation or a meaningful amplification: the endpoint is authenticated, globally rate-limited per user, input-bounded, and cost-bounded.
record.claimed_root_cause: Pattern preview performs a server-side render on every request with only the global user throttle (1000/day) and no dedicated throttle scope or cache, so it is claimed to be an unbounded/under-throttled render cost.

trace.description: @action(detail=True, url_path='preview') calls preview_pattern(pattern, theme, accent, style) per request; no throttle_classes override and no cache lookup.
Only action 'default' is switched to PublicReadThrottle; preview uses super().get_throttles() -> DEFAULT_THROTTLE_CLASSES.
ResilientAnonRateThrottle + ResilientUserRateThrottle with 'anon':'100/day', 'user':'1000/day', 'public_read':'1000/hour'; no 'design_preview' or similar scope exists.
Authenticated requests key the 'user' scope by request.user.pk; anonymous requests fall back to IP. ResilientUserRateThrottle only adds fail-open cache behavior (DaventProject/throttling.py:91-96).
CODE_MAX=200_000 and validate_html/css/js bound each stored markup field; variables are sanitized by clean_pattern_variables and render escapes non-list values (models.py:358-380).

Per-request render uses fixed SAMPLE_PRODUCTS/CATEGORIES/SERVICES, sanitize_markup(pattern.render(sample_context(), raw=raw)), theme_css+SURFACE_CSS+pattern.css through sanitize_css, and returns raw pattern.js; cost is proportional to bounded stored markup, not to request count beyond the 1000/day/user cap.

evidence.description: preview action has no throttle_classes and no cache; it is the only per-request markup render endpoint in the design viewset.
catalog_cached() exists for catalog/default payloads only; preview does not use it, confirming the 'no cache' observation but also showing cache is not part of the catalog contract.
_ResilientThrottleMixin fails open on cache errors; ResilientUserRateThrottle is the class actually applied to authenticated preview requests.
Sample context is constant and small (8 products, 5 categories, 4 services); no tenant data or unbounded query is rendered.
openPatternPreview calls designApi.patternPreview once per user-initiated 'Ver este diseño' click; there is no automatic polling or fan-out.
validate_html/css/js enforce CODE_MAX=200_000 per field, bounding single-request input size.

record.reason: The observation (no dedicated throttle scope/cache) is accurate but does not establish a security issue. The endpoint is authenticated, inherits a concrete per-user rate limit (1000/day keyed by user.pk), accepts only bounded markup fields (200k chars each), renders a constant sample context, sanitizes output, and has no amplification fan-out or cache-stamp cost. Whether 1000 renders/day is operationally meaningful depends on deployment capacity and account-creation economics — runtime facts — but even granting them, this remains an authenticated API within the platform's normal throttling budget rather than a trust-boundary violation. Recommendation is hardening only: add a dedicated throttle scope and/or cache keyed by pattern revision+theme+style if profiling shows preview cost matters.

record.title: sync/run reaches publish_design_draft without a direct has_customization gate, but draft writes are gated and public render/serializer re-filter — no unauthorized effective publish
record.description: Verified the plumbing: POST /api/stores/sync/run/ resolves only the caller's own Store (user__user=request.user) and calls run_sync, which calls publish_design_draft when design_draft_pending. Unlike customization_publish/discard/restore and the customization PATCH, sync_run and the sync GET have no profile_has_benefit check. publish_design_draft copies layout_config_draft->layout_config and site_theme_draft->site_theme verbatim and only re-checks template_draft against allowed_templates_of before publishing. The claimed impact is nevertheless refuted on current source. (1) Owner-scoped: no cross-store IDOR. (2) Drafts are not freely writable: customization PATCH requires has_customization and validates layout_config via clean_layout_config and site_theme via clean_site_theme against current benefits; AI-design apply requires has_customization+has_ai_design and cleans layout before writing drafts. (3) Plan coupling: every seeded plan sets has_public_link=True together with has_customization=True, and plan_benefits_of returns {} unless suscription.grants_access(), so an expired/inactive subscription yields no benefits and the public endpoint 404s on has_public_link while allowed_templates_of collapses to ('raiz',). (4) Even if a stale premium draft is published, the public read path re-filters: StoreCustomizationPublicSerializer.to_representation runs filter_site_theme by current has_design_plus/has_design_advanced/has_customization and recomputes site_templates/show_catalog; the public store endpoint requires has_public_link; render_store_pattern re-checks template and site_theme.style.id against allowed_templates_of; and layout_config's premium/ai_only blocks are inert because clean_layout_config drops them at write time and the live frontend templateBlocks() only overlays saved values onto canonical template blocks (non-canonical ids are dropped). The prior catalog layout read-drift candidate was already rejected for exactly this dead-sink reason. The missing has_customization check on sync_run/sync GET is a real consistency/defense-in-depth gap, but it does not produce a demonstrated unauthorized public change under the shipped plan catalog.
record.claimed_root_cause: POST /api/stores/sync/run/ reaches run_sync -> publish_design_draft, which copies design drafts to published fields without the explicit profile_has_benefit('has_customization') check enforced by sibling publish/restore/customization paths.

trace.description: POST /api/stores/sync/run/ -> get_object_or_404(Store, user__user=request.user) then Response(run_sync(store)); no profile_has_benefit gate (GET sync at 1726-1731 is likewise ungated but read-only).
If design_draft_pending(store) it calls publish_design_draft(store, note='Sincronización manual') then marks pending StoreSyncEvents done.

Copies layout_config_draft->layout_config and site_theme_draft->site_theme verbatim; template_draft is published only if it remains in allowed_templates_of(store.user), then template_draft is aligned to the resulting template and a StudioVersion snapshot is written.

Public store 404s without has_public_link (637-639); StoreCustomizationPublicSerializer filters site_theme/site_templates by current benefits (serializers.py:724-736); render_store_pattern re-checks template/style.id (pattern_render.py:1766-1773,1799-1807); layout_config premium/ai blocks are inert in the live renderer (frontend/templates/index.js:119-137).

evidence.description: customization PUT/PATCH requires profile_has_benefit(store.user,'has_customization') and discards premium fields by current benefits before serializer validation.
PATCH also drops template/template_draft outside allowed_templates_of(store.user).
validate_layout_config/validate_layout_config_draft run clean_layout_config with current has_design_advanced/has_ai_design, dropping premium and ai_only blocks at write time.

_clean_theme/validate_site_theme run clean_site_theme with plan flags and merge over stored; clean_site_theme also strips style.id when its template is outside allowed_templates_of (site_theme.py:650-664).

customization_publish requires has_customization before calling the same publish_design_draft; discard (1617) and restore (1654) also gate has_customization, with restore scoping StudioVersion by store and re-checking template at 1683.
ai-design/apply requires has_customization and has_ai_design before apply_ai_design writes drafts (ai_design.py:3095-3108) and publishes via the same draft->published copy (ai_design.py:2914-2937).
dict_plan_benefits: every shipped plan (basico/estandar/premium/ecommerce) sets has_public_link=True and has_customization=True; no seeded plan grants public link without customization.

Suscription.grants_access() requires status active and now <= end_date(+grace); plan_benefits_of returns {} without it, so expired/inactive users lose all benefit-gated surfaces including has_public_link.
Public store endpoint raises Http404 unless profile_has_benefit(store.user,'has_public_link'); the same check guards public_contact and the pattern document family.

StoreCustomizationPublicSerializer.to_representation filters site_theme via filter_site_theme(has_plus/has_advanced/has_style), caps videos, clears live_stream_url/accent when benefits lapse, and recomputes site_templates/show_catalog.
render_store_pattern re-checks customization.template against _allowed_templates_safe and falls back to the default pattern; style.id is re-validated against allowed templates at 1799-1807.

templateBlocks() iterates only the template's canonical blocks.<surface> and overlays saved enabled/variant/props onto matching ids; non-canonical ids (including ai_* and the premium catalog 'banner' that is not in CATALOG_BLOCKS) are dropped.
clean_layout_config/_clean_blocks discards unknown/duplicate ids and drops spec['premium'] blocks without has_design_advanced and spec['ai_only'] blocks without has_ai_design at write time.

record.reason: The missing direct has_customization check on sync_run (and the read-only sync GET) is a genuine consistency gap worth hardening, but the claimed security impact does not hold on current source. The path is owner-scoped; every shipped plan couples has_public_link with has_customization; an inactive/expired subscription yields no benefits and the public web 404s; draft mutations are only reachable through has_customization/has_ai_design-gated writes that sanitize layout_config/site_theme; publish_design_draft still re-checks template_draft against the live plan whitelist; and the public serializer/render path re-filters theme, templates, and pattern selection while non-canonical/premium layout blocks are inert in the live renderer. A residual would require an out-of-catalog plan granting has_public_link without has_customization or direct DB manipulation — an admin/config anomaly, not a source-proven trust-boundary violation.
